PullRequest.Title: mcp: discover Copilot CLI user MCP config by default without forwarding it
PullRequest.Body:

Part of #340161. Together with #340034, fixes #339955.

Servers migrated from user `mcp.json` to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` stopped showing up in local chat. This PR makes the local harness discover that file by default, without forwarding its servers to other agents or hosts. The workspace `.mcp.json` side (accepting `"type": "local"`) is handled in #340034.

## Changes

**`~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` is discovered by default**

Migration moves user-level servers into the Copilot CLI user config, but the `copilot` source of `chat.mcp.discovery.enabled` was off by default.

- Added `defaultDiscoverySourceEnablement`, with only `copilot: true`. Claude Desktop, Cursor and Windsurf stay off.
- Added `isDiscoverySourceEnabled`, used by `_isDiscoveryEnabled`. A source the user hasn't set falls back to its default. An explicit `false` and the legacy boolean form are still respected.
- The configuration service deep-merges a partial user value (e.g. `{ "claude-desktop": true }`) with the default object, so `copilot` stays on in that case too.
- Updated the setting description.

**Copilot-home servers are never forwarded to other agents or hosts**

- The same-machine Copilot CLI session still reads the file itself (`RuntimeDiscovered`).
- In every other agent-host session (Claude, Codex, or Copilot on another remote authority) they are `NotDelivered`, with a new `CopilotHomeNotForwarded` reason and message.
- This keeps literal `env` and header credentials in `mcp-config.json` from being copied to another provider or machine without approval, now that the source is on by default.

## Notes for reviewers

- **Duplicates:** with the default `chat.mcp.collisionBehavior: disable`, a server with the same name in user `mcp.json` (order 200) takes priority, and the `mcp-config.json` copy (order 400) is disabled.
- **Servers appearing for existing CLI users:** people with servers in `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json` will now see them in local chat. This includes the remote machine's file in remote windows. These servers are trusted only after the user approves them, so expect a trust prompt.
- **Lost forwarding:** users who had opted in to the `copilot` source lose forwarding of these servers to Claude/Codex sessions and other remote hosts.
- **Explicit opt-outs:** users who set `"copilot": false`, or the legacy `false`, will still not see their migrated user servers.

## How to test

1. With `chat.mcp.discovery.enabled` unset, add a server to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`. It should appear as "GitHub Copilot CLI".
2. Set `chat.mcp.discovery.enabled` to `{ "copilot": false }` or `false`. The server should disappear.
3. Open a Claude or Codex agent-host session. The Copilot-home server should show as unsupported with the "not shared with other agents or remote hosts" explanation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed
- `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`: passed
- `./scripts/test.sh --reporter dot --run src/vs/platform/mcp/test/common/mcpWorkspaceConfiguration.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/mcp/test/common/mcpResourceScannerService.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/workspaceDotMcpDiscovery.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/test/common/nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/agentHostMcpServerSupport.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/agentSessions/resolveCustomizationRefs.test.ts --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/mcpServerCustomizationMigration.test.ts`: 181 passing
- `npm run eslint -- <changed files>`: clean

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup with chat.mcp.discovery.enabled unset, locally and in a remote window
Scenarios.CriticalPath: MCP discovery starts at WorkbenchPhase.AfterRestored, so it does not block workbench restoration. The async native-helper load must complete before discovery installs watchers; the Copilot config file read, JSON adaptation, and per-server nonce hashes must complete before its servers appear.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load native MCP discovery environment data from the main process or remote agent.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once for the local discovery instance and, when connected remotely, once for the remote discovery instance.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The helper was loaded regardless of whether Copilot discovery was enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Asynchronous and after restoration; discovery setup waits for it, but the workbench does not.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create a non-recursive watcher and read mcp-config.json.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher and one initial read per active machine side, so one locally and at most one additional remote-side pair in a remote window.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: With the setting unset, the Copilot source was disabled, so no Copilot-home watcher or initial read was created; explicit opt-in performed the same work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the restore critical path; server availability waits for the read and adaptation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The file read scales with config bytes and adaptation/hash work scales linearly with the number and size of configured servers; machine-side watcher cardinality remains bounded at one per local/remote side.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One Copilot watcher/read runs for the local side; a remote window can also run one for the remote side. Each file is read once initially. Definitions are hashed concurrently with Promise.all, with cardinality equal to servers in that one config file.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no parsed-content cache. A missing file produces an empty result after one failed initial read while the watcher remains for future creation; successful definitions remain in the registered observable collection until a change, disable, or disposal.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed default directly enables the existing watcher/read path, and its phase, cardinality, and async call path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Real Copilot config sizes vary, but typical files contain few servers; no evidence shows the bounded after-restored read/hash work causing noticeable latency.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new work is the intended discovery feature, is bounded to one file per machine side, occurs after restoration, and has no evidenced user-visible performance impact.

Scenarios.Scenario: Copilot MCP configuration changes while the workbench is running or discovery is toggled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A file event schedules updateFile; the read, parse, and hashes must finish before the observable server definitions and registry reflect the edit. Disabling the source synchronously clears the collection and disposes the autorun-owned scheduler/watcher.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-read the complete mcp-config.json after watcher notifications.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one scheduled read per 500 ms event burst per local/remote config watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same coalesced refresh occurred only after explicit Copilot-source opt-in; default-unset users had no watcher.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Only discovery freshness waits; general UI progress does not.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost scales with edit bursts, config bytes, and server count after coalescing; it does not fan out into per-server filesystem calls.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces watcher events within 500 ms independently per machine side. Per-server SHA-256 hashes within one refresh run concurrently. Slow refreshes could overlap with later scheduled refreshes, but that behavior pre-existed for explicitly enabled discovery and the diff does not alter scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No warm parse cache is used, but watcher events are coalesced. Disabling or disposing discovery releases the watcher and registration; re-enabling performs a fresh read.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the refresh and cleanup mechanics; low that realistic inputs make them a performance regression.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: External tools' save patterns and unusually large server lists are unknown. The bounded one-file refresh gives no concrete evidence of jank or excessive I/O.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. Coalescing and lifecycle cleanup are present, and the diff changes the default reachability rather than introducing repeated per-item I/O or an unbounded resource.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent-host support assessment and customization publication for Copilot-home servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: During active-client customization resolution, all discovered MCP servers are classified. Matching same-machine Copilot CLI sessions return RuntimeDiscovered immediately. Every other agent or host now returns NotDelivered immediately, before projection, variable resolution, serialization, or standalone bundle creation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize forwarded MCP servers into a synthetic .mcp.json and compute bundle content/nonces.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Before the diff, one grouped standalone bundle contained all forwarded Copilot-home servers for the session; after the diff, these servers contribute zero entries and may avoid the bundle entirely when no standalone files remain.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Copilot-home servers not runtime-discovered by the target were projected and forwarded as one synthetic bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Bundling is awaited before publishing customization refs; this change removes rather than adds that work for non-owner sessions.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write the synthetic bundle manifest and .mcp.json to the in-memory customization filesystem.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one manifest and one .mcp.json write per changed grouped bundle; now zero writes attributable to Copilot-home servers, and zero bundle calls when they were the only standalone content.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Non-owner Copilot-home servers could trigger or enlarge the standalone bundle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Previously awaited on active-client publication; removed by the changed delivery decision.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Classification remains linear in all discovered MCP servers. Removed serialization scales with the count and configuration size of Copilot-home servers after grouping into one bundle.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Server classifications are launched with Promise.all across the discovered server set. The new Copilot-home branch itself performs no asynchronous boundary work, and non-owner servers no longer contribute to bundling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The bundler has a content nonce and reuses an unchanged prior bundle; the changed path bypasses it for Copilot-home servers. Runtime discovery continues to use the watched config on the owning machine.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed branch returns before projection and tests establish zero Copilot-home bundling for non-owner sessions.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The amount of avoided bundle work depends on server count and whether other standalone customizations still require a bundle.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. This path reduces serialization, virtual-filesystem writes, and forwarded bytes while preserving the same-machine runtime-discovery path.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 10 changed files and relevant transitive discovery, registry, hashing, agent-host resolution, and bundling paths. The PR intentionally adds one bounded post-restore Copilot config watcher/read per machine side and removes non-owner forwarding/bundling. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
